root_cause.text: The IPv4 multipath hash seed sysctl code treated an 8-byte `struct sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed` as a single atomic object in `READ_ONCE()`/`WRITE_ONCE()`, which caused Clang LTO to emit misaligned 64-bit acquire loads on a 4-byte-aligned ARM64 field and also allowed non-atomic torn writes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `fib_multipath_hash_from_keys()` from `READ_ONCE(net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed).mp_seed` to `READ_ONCE(net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed.mp_seed)`, explicitly splits `WRITE_ONCE(net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed, new)` into two 32-bit writes to `user_seed` and `mp_seed`, and adds `READ_ONCE(mphs->user_seed)` in `proc_fib_multipath_hash_seed()`, matching the CVE description that the full-struct `READ_ONCE()` became a 64-bit `ldar` on an unaligned address under Clang LTO and triggered an ARM64 alignment fault.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the multipath hash seed read to correctly access the `mp_seed` field through READ_ONCE.
intent_record.what: The code changes the READ_ONCE access from `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed).mp_seed` to `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed.mp_seed`, moving the `.mp_seed` field selection inside the argument passed to READ_ONCE.
intent_record.how: This makes the read operate on the `mp_seed` field of the `sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed` structure as a single expression, ensuring the intended seed value is fetched atomically/safely from the struct member instead of applying the field access after the READ_ONCE result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the multipath hash seed fields individually to ensure correct and safe runtime writes.
intent_record.what: The assignment to `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed` was split into two `WRITE_ONCE()` operations: one writing `new.user_seed` into `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed.user_seed`, and a second writing `new.mp_seed` into `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed.mp_seed`, replacing the previous single struct-wide assignment.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the two seed fields are now updated individually rather than replacing the whole structure in one write. This preserves field-specific updates and avoids a potentially problematic full-structure overwrite, improving concurrent visibility of each member.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use READ_ONCE() when reading the multipath hash seed to avoid unsafe concurrent access to the sysctl value.
intent_record.what: The assignment to `user_seed` was changed from a direct read of `mphs->user_seed` to `READ_ONCE(mphs->user_seed)` inside `proc_fib_multipath_hash_seed()`.
intent_record.how: This makes the read of `user_seed` atomic with respect to compiler optimizations and concurrent access, ensuring the function observes a single coherent value of the sysctl field while it is being copied into the temporary table structure.

candidates.rationale: This treats the entire 8-byte sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed struct as one atomic object. On ARM64 with 4-byte alignment, this can trigger misaligned 64-bit accesses under Clang LTO and also permits torn non-atomic writes, which matches the root cause.
This direct field read accesses the shared multipath hash seed structure without READ_ONCE on the specific field, which is the kind of unsafe concurrent access the fix is correcting.

This line shows the vulnerable pre-fix pattern that was changed to a safe field-wise access. The root cause is the atomic object-level read of the whole struct, which is unsafe for an 8-byte object on 4-byte-aligned ARM64.

vuln_statements.explanation: This reads the entire 8-byte sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed object via READ_ONCE() and then accesses a field, which can force a misaligned 64-bit access under Clang LTO on 4-byte-aligned ARM64 and reflects the unsafe whole-object atomic access described in the root cause.

This writes the entire 8-byte sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed object with WRITE_ONCE(), which can generate torn non-atomic writes and the same misaligned 64-bit access problem for a 4-byte-aligned field.
This directly reads a shared field from the multipath hash seed structure without READ_ONCE() on the field, allowing unsafe concurrent access to the sysctl value.
